questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Living in a metropole, learning the language, learning the academic culture, getting to know Paris, getting to know french culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, the information was ok, but at times it seemed unclear who was responsible for each domain in the administration causing a lot of futile emailing back and forth.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received e-mails about important dates and then there was an online introductory meeting on how to do the course inscription.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived at the Cité Universitaire

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there was a common kitchen in the house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The Cité Universitaire is a very privileged place to live because of the low rent and good facilities. On the other hand it's not the real Paris experience as it feels a little like an international student ghetto at times.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit tiresome because you had to read across several documents instead of just one when putting together your schedule. Also the relevant documents were not always easy to find on the website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails and an online meeting.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I had all the courses I applied for and, I realize having received my transcript of records, even one I didn't apply for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a messy experience but be indulgent and patient and all will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 5 third year courses. The academic level was similar to the one at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: To a great extent, lectures and seminars at Sorbonne are based on one-way communication from the professor. This has it's advantages as the academic ground covered this way becomes larger, but on the other hand it doesn't activate the students as much.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Littérature et cinéma
Littérature classique et moderne
Écrire et penser la fiction
Patrimoine culturel de la France
La peinture en Europe, 1650-1750

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the first to courses (Littérature et cinéma and Littérature classique et moderne) the most because the professor who taught these courses were really good and really seemed to care if we understood the subject matter or not.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Local transportation was a bit expensive I think. Bakeries and small grocery stores are cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to the Parismus events a couple of times.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to do some kind of sport. I did a bit of bouldering which was a good way to get to talk to some new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do small trips in France. The train tickets are really cheap and the TGV-trains are so fast that you can get to almost any french city within a couple of hours.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: At first even just finding out where to do your grocery shopping and what to eat for each meal was a bit exhausting, but you quickly get a routine and get tips from others.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most of them are open to talk if you take the initiative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I often found french rules and administrative procedures overly bureaucratic.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The life and the buzz in the streets and in the bars, cafés and restaurants.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You have to figure out a fair amount of paper work to actually get to study, but just take it easy, you'll be fine.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that you're an exchange student and don't have to live up to quite the same standards as the french students and as back home. You'll learn a lot just by being there and by completing the courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To become friends with some french speaking people and do small trips and soirées with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having a network of actual friends around you and relying a lot on superficial relations.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
